item.text: With the specified 25 mm cell size, the initial atlas points to mass-in-frame resonators as candidates. The targets are near the estimated feasibility boundary; I’m refining the search before checking a candidate with the certification solver.

The search found a sphere-and-ligament resonator estimated at 18.5% relative density, 50.9 MPa cube-axis modulus, and a complete gap spanning 10.76–30.44 kHz. These are preliminary values; certification is now checking whether it meets all three targets with numerical error bounds.
Certification is still running. It checks stiffness across multiple mesh resolutions and searches the full Brillouin zone for the gap, including wave directions outside the usual symmetry paths.
The certificate has not returned yet. I’m keeping the requested limits fixed and will release a design only if the guarded results satisfy all of them.
The certification solve is still in progress, with no verdict available yet. The search result remains provisional.

The material model uses isotropic PA12 with Young’s modulus 1.7 GPa, Poisson’s ratio 0.39, and density 1,010 kg/m³. The pending certificate concerns infinite-lattice performance; it does not assess SLS printability.
Certification is taking longer than the preliminary search and is still running. I’m waiting for its stiffness and full-zone gap verdict before submitting the outcome.
